presentation.title: Guided-cassette preliminary design
presentation.focus: Play the match replays in the motion list for the whole cycle: six floor NOTES scored, then the climb. The mechanism cases above them are the checked discharge, the service-pin withdrawal and the displaced control.
notes: Release 003-1 is the release 003 design in one view. The layout, limits, budgets, checked cases and trial data are unchanged; the four match replays now play in this page's motion list.

The layout check covers one NOTE discharge (0.3 s of the 96-segment trial) and the service-pin withdrawal. The match replays are recorded playback of the pinned trial files. They are not clearance cases and the decision does not depend on them.

Cam rise is kinematic. From belt enable, a free torus responds to compliant tread contact, motor current, gravity and field surfaces. The held cassette starts both belts from rest. Air drag, actual friction and finished inertia remain unmeasured.

Free chassis on unilateral tire and bumper contacts. Twenty-four articulated chain links connect two field anchors. Two ideal gate constraints engage inside a 12 mm capture window. The pivot has a 215 N·m limit. Motor torque goes to zero at 4 s. The brake holds for the remaining 5 s.

Field meshes are reduced from FE-2024.STEP in its registered coordinates. The physics uses separate original speaker surfaces and a lumped chain. The colored opening outline marks the actual scoring plane.
Nominal foam compression is represented by the two rigid tread/NOTE overlaps. Six post reliefs clear the outer tread return. Baseline and failing trials are retained locally.

Drive screen uses 50 A motor limit per side, direct pulleys, 0.20 kg effective moving mass per belt and assumed grip. At the sensor-registered placement, the 0.18 and 0.22 kg cases also register. Moving the robot 120 mm downfield misses registration in the tested coarse run.

The ideal hook constraint starts from a chain within 12 mm of each throat. Gate capture from a driving approach, clearance to every truss member, air drag and drive hardware are open. The suspended chassis continues swinging during the disabled interval.

Shovel stock is nominally 3.0 mm above the flat carpet. Swing bumper clearance bound 85.2 mm; front reach bound 642.3 mm against the 644.8 mm project envelope. Up to 21.3 mm extra slide retraction. Complete truck support, fasteners, wear and loaded flex remain open.
The shaft moved 58 mm toward the mouth and 12 mm above the old axis. The raised ends of both lid rails support it. The spring and stop are preliminary parameters.
Profile A is the default. At fixed pivot height, 0.384° of extra nose-down pitch uses the nominal 3.0 mm floor clearance. Measure loaded pitch, wear and carpet variation on the physical nose.

Bounded risk experiment 01. The staged shot scored on both numerical refinements. The raised stop traded reduced digging for a missed high-side pickup. The finite friction brake slipped at all three CG positions. The five Trial replays use the same assembled robot.

Catch stock, fasteners and actuator reserve add 0.263–0.453 kg. A 2 A peak allowance is included in the electrical ledger. Rigid dog contact was verified against the modeled normal face; a 1° overrotation enters it. Earlier angular-spring trials are retained as controls.

Two chain hooks capture before the shared pivot motor reels. After both slide stops seat, the drive unloads the cable and a passive take-up keeps it tensioned. The spring package is a purchasing allowance.
